quote: Henry Crane standing as if he were a model of restraint
Henry's grief read public and sharp; he held himself with the taut courtesy of someone who thinks performance protects feeling.
Henry's hands were clenched in his pockets; "In the morning room — same chair by the hearth; I was reading the paper. Ask Marta; she brought my tea."
